claims.explanation: The drug AM-92016 is annotated as a potassium channel blocker and an oxypropanolamine analogue of sotalol, but the selective killing pattern across cell lines is best explained by loss of PTEN and/or TP53, which are the most recurrent alterations in the sensitive lines. PTEN loss and TP53 mutation are known to impair DNA damage responses and increase dependence on pro-survival signaling, potentially sensitizing cells to ion-channel blockade and downstream stress. The protective effect of BRAF/NRAS mutations in melanoma and other lines suggests that MAPK pathway activation may reduce dependence on the drug's target pathway.

features.basis: PTEN loss is enriched in sensitive lines (ZR751, KALS1, OV7) and impairs survival signaling
TP53 mutation is highly recurrent in sensitive lines and may impair stress responses
BRAF-mutant melanoma lines are among least affected, suggesting MAPK-driven resistance
NRAS-mutant lines (IPC298, KU1919) show mixed but mostly resistant pattern
EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines (HCC4006, NCIH1650, KYSE270) are sensitive
KRAS-mutant lines appear more often in resistant group (HGC27, T3M4, CL11)
CDKN2A loss co-occurs with sensitivity in melanoma and other lines
ARID1A mutation seen in sensitive lines (LOXIMVI, KU1919) but also resistant, weak evidence
NF1 mutation appears in several resistant lines (BICR6, S117, FTC133)
PIK3CA mutation enriched in resistant lines (HGC27, SNU840, SNUC5)
FBXW7 mutation in sensitive lines (NCIH1648, MKN1) but also resistant, weak
SMARCA4 mutation in sensitive lines (OV7, KYSE270) but limited evidence
